name: run_read_query

input.cypher:
MATCH (s:Supplier)<-[:RFQ_FROM_SUPPLIER]-(rfq:RFQ)
WITH s, count(rfq) AS TotalRFQs,
     count(CASE WHEN (rfq)<-[:IS_SUPPLIER_REJECTED_RFQ_STATE]-() THEN 1 END) AS RejectedRFQs
WHERE TotalRFQs > 0
RETURN s.CompanyName, TotalRFQs, RejectedRFQs, round(100.0 * RejectedRFQs / TotalRFQs, 1) AS RejectionRatePct
ORDER BY RejectedRFQs DESC, RejectionRatePct DESC

text:
**Norske Meierier** has the most rejected quotes, both in count and as a share of its quotes. The Buyer rejected 3 of its 8 quotes (37.5%).

| Supplier | Quotes received | Rejected | Rejection rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| Norske Meierier | 8 | 3 | 37.5% |
| Grandma Kelly's Homestead | 6 | 2 | 33.3% |
| PB Knäckebröd AB | 3 | 1 | 33.3% |
| Zaanse Snoepfabriek | 3 | 1 | 33.3% |
| Mayumi's, Heli Süßwaren, Bigfoot Breweries, Ma Maison | 4 each | 1 each | 25% |

Eight more suppliers have one rejection each, at rates of 16.7–20%. Another 13 suppliers have had no rejections.

Most suppliers have only 1–8 quotes, so one rejection moves the rate a lot. PB Knäckebröd and Zaanse Snoepfabriek sit at 33% on just 3 quotes each.

These figures are a live snapshot, and the simulation keeps changing them.

I used the template `supplier_reliability_rfq_rejection_rate`. I changed the sort order to put the rejection count first.
How many POs are waiting for approval?

input.cypher:
MATCH (:NewPoS)-[:IS_NEW_PO_STATE]->(po:PurchaseOrder)
OPTIONAL MATCH (po)-[i:HAS_PO_ITEM]->(p:Product)
WITH po, sum(i.POqt * p.UnitPrice * i.POPriceDiscount) AS cost
RETURN count(po) AS NewPOs, round(sum(cost),2) AS TotalValue, round(min(cost),2) AS MinCost, round(max(cost),2) AS MaxCost
